value.reason: The flagged field, SecurityQuestionId (models/securityAnswer.ts:33-35), is an INTEGER foreign key. It only records which predefined security question the user picked. It is not the authentication secret. The secret is the answer, and that is a separate attribute (datacreator.ts:707 creates the record with { SecurityQuestionId, UserId, answer }). The data flow also shows the chosen question is meant to be shown to users: routes/securityQuestion.ts returns it as part of the password-reset flow. So encrypting or masking this ID would not protect any secret. Encrypting a foreign key would also break the relational join for no security gain. The positive example flags a sensitive value (a card number) stored as a plain integer. This case is different: it's a non-secret reference ID. The Terraform EFS and SQLite storage snippets are general storage context and don't show that this field holds sensitive authentication data. Missing-encryption rules (CWE-311, DPDP Rule 6(1)(a)) don't apply to this field. Any real concern would be about how the 'answer' attribute is stored, and that is not what this finding flags.
